assets.applicability: Typed TypeScript projects whose requirements can be expressed through compiler-visible types.
assets.contribution: TypeScript checks can deterministically reject type-level contract violations.
assets.evidence_basis: TypeScript compiler checks are an existing deterministic mechanism when the requirement is type-expressible.
limitations: Runtime behavior and editorial quality are outside the type system.
Coverage depends on compiler settings and available declarations.
assets.name: TypeScript type checks

assets.applicability: JavaScript and TypeScript source where repository lint configuration is available.
assets.contribution: Existing ESLint rules can be selected and configured to enforce supported source-code constraints.
assets.evidence_basis: ESLint is represented as a configurable capability family; later evidence must identify applicable rules and settings.
limitations: Configuration cannot enforce requirements for which no applicable rule or parser support exists.
Project-specific semantics can still require a plugin or repository validator.
assets.name: ESLint configuration
